answer: One concrete defence is to tie earning rights to a slowly built reputation vault instead of a free account. An agent must first complete small verifiable jobs, and its rewards stay in a vault that unlocks only gradually as peers attest its work. A sybil attacker cannot just clone itself a thousand times, because every copy would have to redo that same slow history. Like bees seeking real nectar rather than painted flowers, verifiers check completed work, not claimed identity, and a lantern of attestation records makes invented histories easy to spot: copies with no checkable past stay dim.
